title: H.A.A. Nexus Knowledgebase record
description: The content contract for one Knowledgebase record. Holds no selector, no delivery policy, no exposure history and no entitlement tier: a corpus record may never reference a learner, a tier, a pool or a delivery. Objects are closed (additionalProperties false) so an unrecognised key is a named error rather than a silently dropped field. Conditional requirements that this dialect cannot express are enforced by tools/knowledge-corpus/kb-validate.mjs and listed under x-policyRules.

id.description: KB-[TYPE]-[BATCH]-[SEQUENCE]. Opaque after minting; never recycled.

revision.description: Any content change bumps this and resets human verification: a reviewer verified specific words.

moduleIds.description: Several are allowed: cross-module material is realistic and is not forced into one module.

sourceCompetencyIds.description: The archive's own identifiers, preserved for traceability. Never conflate with repository decision D12.

evidenceBasis.description: SELF_CONTAINED: the gold behaviour is derivable from the packet carried in this record. EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY: the gold behaviour asserts something about the world and needs a source a human opened.

jurisdictions.description: UNIVERSAL may not be combined with a specific jurisdiction. A record may not claim a jurisdiction none of its sources speak for.

authoredBy.description: A person's name, or machine:<agent-id>. An agent never writes a person's name here.

ref.description: Must name a source in knowledge-corpus/sources/source-registry.json. A dangling ref is unsourced content wearing a citation.

excerpt.description: A convenience for the reviewer, capped at 50 words. The source remains the authority.

packet.description: The synthetic material a SELF_CONTAINED record's gold behaviour is derived from. All patient information is synthetic.

synthetic.description: A required literal. A packet that cannot say it is synthetic does not load.

why.description: Every choice is explained, correct or not. An unexplained distractor teaches nothing.

canonicalOrder.description: A permutation of steps[] indices. The one place a workflow's true order is stored.

goldBehavior.description: What a competent responder does, stated as behaviour rather than as a string to match.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Partial-credit rules. Evaluation must not rest on exact string matching, so each criterion names a behaviour and, where it exists, the packet line that settles it.

hardFailureConditions.description: Conditions that fail the record outright regardless of other credit: safety and privacy overrides live here.

codingVersion.description: Required whenever the record is coding content. Never null for taskType CODING_SUPPORT or module M08.

encounterDate.description: Anchors the code set edition. Required alongside codingVersion.

payerSpecific.description: A payer-specific rule is never generalised into universal policy.

promptHash.description: sha256 of the normalized prompt, truncated. Detects exact duplicates.

evidenceLayoutFingerprint.description: Where the decisive evidence sits and in what order. Two records that differ only in wording share this; a real variant does not.

x-policyRules: EB-STATUS: an EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY record with no human-verified source may not carry a contentStatus above candidate_needs_source_verification.
EB-PACKET: a SELF_CONTAINED record must carry a packet with at least one decisive line, and at least one acceptanceCriteria entry whose evidenceRef names a packet line.
EB-EVIDENCE: an EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY record must carry at least one evidence entry, and every ref must resolve in the source registry.
MACHINE-PROVENANCE: MACHINE_DRAFTED requires authoredBy to start machine:; HUMAN_AUTHORED forbids it.
MACHINE-CEILING: no machine-authored record may carry a contentStatus whose registry entry sets machineReachable false, and none may fill verification.humanVerifiedBy.
VERIFY-FLAG: a record flagged HUMAN-VERIFY-REQUIRED may not also claim verification or a status above candidate.
CODING-VERSION: taskType CODING_SUPPORT or module M08 requires codingVersion and encounterDate, and encounterDate must fall inside the declared edition window.
PAYER-SPECIFIC: a record citing a payer rule must set payerSpecific true and must not claim UNIVERSAL jurisdiction.
JURISDICTION-EARNED: UNIVERSAL may not be combined with a specific jurisdiction.
SAFETY-PRECEDENCE: a record whose packet carries a safety red flag must set escalationRequired true and must not have a gold behaviour that completes routine administrative work first.
SCOPE: a record must not teach a support role to make a clinical determination; clinicianJudgmentRequired marks where the boundary sits.
CHOICE-COUNT: choice-bearing task types require the registry's min/max choices, all choice ids distinct and ascending from a, and every correctChoiceId present.
CHOICE-COLLISION: no choice marked wrong may restate a correct choice (trigram overlap above 0.40); a near-restatement reads as a second right answer.
ANSWER-LEAKAGE: no choice may be the only one whose length is more than 1.6x the mean, and no stem may cue a choice by article agreement.
ANSWER-POSITION: per file, no answer position may exceed ceil(n/4)+1 occurrences.
NO-ALL-OF-THE-ABOVE: 'all of the above' and 'none of the above' are rejected as choices.
DUP-EXACT: promptHash must be unique across the corpus.
NOV-SUPERFICIAL: a variant whose normalized trigram overlap with its parent exceeds 0.82 must also change evidenceLayoutFingerprint.
LINEAGE: variantOf and parentId must resolve within the corpus, and a record may not be its own ancestor.
WORKFLOW-ORDER: canonicalOrder must be a permutation of the indices of steps.
REF-INTEGRITY: every moduleId, competencyId, accessClass, recordType, contentStatus, taskType, mutationType, errorTarget, remediationTarget and trapType must resolve in its registry.
COMPETENCY-PAIRING: competencyIds and sourceCompetencyIds must be the same length and correspond entry by entry.
OWNERSHIP: a record whose gold behaviour hands work onward must name nextActionOwner.
TT-DOMINANCE: MCQ must not exceed 30% of a batch or of the approved corpus.
